newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DEPLETED RANGERS UNLIKELY TO CAUSE AJAX TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPLETED RANGERS UNLIKELY TO CAUSE AJAX TROUBLE.

text.p: Glasgow Rangers, depleted by injuries and suspensions, will create a major upset on Wednesday night if they beat Ajax to keep alive their faint hopes of survival in the European Champions' League.

Most of the capacity 40,000-plus crowd will go to Ibrox for the Group A match more in hope than expectation that Rangers can not only gain some revenge for their 4-1 defeat in Amsterdam two weeks ago but also salvage something from another season of dashed European ambition following three successive Champions' League defeats.
Rangers manager Walter Smith does not expect his side to perform any miracles.

"We know we have a mountain to climb and our chances of survival are extremely slim but while there is still a chance we can qualify we will have to try and take it," an unconvincing Smith said this week.

Rangers go into the match without four suspended players -- Paul Gascoigne, their top scorer this season with 11 goals who was sent off in Amsterdam, skipper Richard Gough and defenders Alex Cleland and Craig Moore.

If that were not bad enough goalkeeper Andy Goram, defender Alan McLaren, midfielder Stuart McCall and strikers Gordon Durie, Ian Ferguson and Ally McCoist are all injured and there is a doubt over Dutch striker Peter van Vossen.

Smith will have to field youngsters and reserves who are unlikely to be able to do much to bring about Rangers' first win in 12 Champions' League matches dating back to the 1992-93 season when they last won a game at this stage of the competition.
And they can hardly relish facing an Ajax side who are only now beginning to find their form after a slow start to the season.
Ajax, who have six points from three matches and top the group on goal difference from Auxerre and Grasshopper, travelled to Glasgow on Monday without their young Portuguese striker Dani.

Dani scored twice against Rangers in their last match which turned in Ajax's favour after Gascoigne was sent off after 29 minutes. But Van Gaal said he was not being considered because he was not "ripe enough" and other players were in better form.

Van Gaal also has to reshuffle his pack because of injuries. Apart from long-term absentees Danny Blind and Jari Litmanen, wingers Tijani Babangida and Marc Overmars, defenders Frank de Boer, Winston Bogarde and Argentine Mariano Juan are far from fit but not fully ruled out.

But Van Gaal is expected to field, for part of the match at least, Patrick Kluivert. The striker appears to be coming back to his best after a troubled period with off-field problems and a long-term knee injury.
Kluivert has scored twice in two recent appearances as a substitute and, if he does play, should relish the atmosphere and occasion in Glasgow.
